statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, r is the largest integer m with 0 <= m <= len(nums) such that for every residue a with 0 <= a < value, cnt(a) >= the number of integers t with 0 <= t < m and t mod value = a, where cnt(a) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] mod value = a. Equivalently, r is the maximum MEX attainable from nums by any number of operations that add or subtract value to individual elements.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value, so 0 <= x mod value < value.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result; it does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, r <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, there is a choice of pairwise distinct indices i_t, one for each integer t with 0 <= t < r, all in [0, len(nums)), such that nums[i_t] mod value = t mod value for every such t. If r <= 0 the choice is empty.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, there is no choice of pairwise distinct indices i_t, one for each integer t with 0 <= t <= r, all in [0, len(nums)), such that nums[i_t] mod value = t mod value for every such t.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, cnt(r mod value) = floor(r / value), where cnt(a) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] mod value = a, and floor(r / value) is integer division of the non-negative r by positive value.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, if value = 1 then r = len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, if no index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) satisfies nums[i] mod value = 0, then r = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, if len(nums) >= value and for every residue a with 0 <= a < value there is an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] mod value = a, then r >= value.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, if value > 1 and every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) satisfies nums[i] mod value = 0, then r = 1.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: For any two arrays nums and nums2 satisfying the preconditions, if len(nums) = len(nums2) and for every residue a with 0 <= a < value the number of indices i with nums[i] mod value = a equals the number of indices i with nums2[i] mod value = a, then whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns r and find_smallest_integer(nums2, value) returns r2, we have r = r2.
preconditions: All arrays mentioned have length between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; every array element is between -10^9 and 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: For any integer x with -10^9 <= x <= 10^9, let nums2 be the array obtained by appending x to nums. If len(nums) < 100000, then whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns r and find_smallest_integer(nums2, value) returns r2, we have r <= r2.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.

statement: Whenever find_smallest_integer(nums, value) returns a result r, if value > len(nums), then r is the least integer t with 0 <= t <= len(nums) such that either t = len(nums) or no index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) satisfies nums[i] mod value = t.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000; value is between 1 and 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; mod denotes the non-negative remainder modulo value.
